description: Aero Hand dances to the music: listen to what's playing and move the hand along with it so it flows with the song. The agent decides the approach (e.g. beat and tempo tracking plus energy/onsets driving finger waves, pinches and poses; smooth trajectories, nothing jerky). Extend third_party/aero_hand/scripts/performance.py (it already starts a random song from the ¿? playlist). LEFT hand; mind servo temperature over a full song.

results.identified_issue: Root causes in the previous version: (1) MOVES cycled wave→bounce→pinch_walk→pose_hits every 8 bars in a fixed order no matter the audio, so only tempo varied; (2) loudness energy was pinned near 1.0 on real music (the loud_lo/loud_hi range adapted at 0.5 dB/s), so amplitude never varied. The beat tracker itself was fine (locked 82 BPM on Walkin within 8 s). Mic access: verified working from a shell process (MacBook Pro Microphone, ~-33 dB with music at volume 56); could NOT verify the Helping Hands app's TCC grant (no read access to TCC.db) — a denied grant yields silence not an error, so the script now prints MICROPHONE IS SILENT after 4 s if peak < -70 dB. New design: Listener tracks per-band power hits (low<150 Hz, mid, high>2 kHz), busyness (high-band onsets per beat over 2 bars), brightness (spectral centroid), and loudness relative to the song's own median (median reads 0.5; mic level is unknown so absolute loudness is useless). pick_move is a hand-written decision tree with thresholds tuned on three clips only (Walkin and HUMBLE. recorded through the mic, plus a synthetic pad→16th-hats file); thresholds are guesses and hip-hop mostly lands on bounce. Moves switch only at bar lines when two consecutive bars agree and ≥2 bars have passed. Half time kicks in when a beat is under ~0.45 s (50% servo cap). Not run on the real hand this turn. --wav runs the whole pipeline offline for regression.
results.summary: The dance now comes from the song: each bar the hand picks a move from what it hears, and each finger reacts to its own part of the sound, so different songs get different dances.
results.detailed_description: Why it looked fixed: the old dance went wave, bounce, pinch walk, pose hits every 8 bars in the same order for every song, and the loudness reading sat near 100%, so only the tempo changed. The beat tracker was fine; it locked onto real songs within a few seconds. Now, at every bar line, the hand picks a move from what it hears: quiet parts get a slow sway, busy hi-hats get small fast finger ripples, loud parts with heavy kicks get pose hits on the downbeat, kicks get a bounce, bright melodic parts get the thumb tapping each finger, and anything else gets a wave. A move changes only when two bars in a row agree, so it doesn't flicker. On top of the move, each finger flicks when its part of the sound hits: index for hi-hats, middle and ring for snare and voice, pinky for kick and bass. Loudness is now measured against the song's own usual level, so choruses and drops make bigger moves and quiet intros make smaller ones. When a beat is too quick for the 50% speed cap, the moves go to half time. Two songs I recorded through the mic: Walkin (136 BPM) bounced the whole way at its own tempo. HUMBLE. (150 BPM, half time) bounced in the verses and switched to pose hits in the 3 loud sections, at 33 s, 70 s and 87 s. A test file that went from a soft pad to busy hi-hats went sway, then pinch walk, then flutter. Mic: it works from a normal process, but I couldn't check whether macOS granted Helping Hands itself mic access. If it hasn't, macOS sends silence instead of an error, so the app log now shows MICROPHONE IS SILENT after 4 seconds. If you see that line, allow Helping Hands under Privacy & Security, then Microphone. Caveats: the move thresholds are tuned on just those three clips, and most hip-hop will land on bounce with pose hits in the loud parts. I haven't run it on the hand. New: performance.py --wav song.wav dances to a file offline and prints the moves.

results.notes: Jake: run from the Helping Hands Mac app, Dance looks like the same fixed list of moves every time. It must follow the music, so each song gets a different dance (tempo, beat, loudness, sections, onsets driving the moves). Check whether it's falling back to the fixed routine (mic permission under the app? beat tracker not locking?), and make the choreography actually come from the audio, at the 50% speed cap. results.identified_issue: Audio comes from the mic, not system audio: Apple Music streams have no file to analyse, and capturing the output would need BlackHole. Room noise and speaker volume affect it, but loudness is measured against a range that adapts. Tempo comes from autocorrelating 8 s of spectral-flux onsets, biased toward 120 BPM, which can lock at half or double time on some songs. Phase comes from a comb sum over the onsets, and the beat clock is nudged 25% toward it every 0.5 s. Not verified: real-song beat accuracy, the right LEAD_S (0.10 s), whether 50/60 °C limits suit the HLS servos, and whether get_actuator_temperatures (a blocking serial read every 3 s) causes a visible hitch. Duplicate started-event code from earlier commits was removed in the refactor into main().
results.summary: The hand now dances to the song: it listens through the Mac mic, follows the beat and loudness, and moves smoothly until the track ends.
results.detailed_description: Run scripts/performance.sh as before. It starts a random ¿? song, then the hand listens through the MacBook microphone instead of playing a fixed routine. It works out the tempo and where each beat lands, and moves on a beat clock. Every 8 bars it switches move: a wave that rolls from index to pinky every two beats, a bounce that dips on each beat, a pinch walk where the thumb taps one fingertip per beat, and pose hits that land peace, rock on, shaka and I love you on each bar's downbeat. Moves crossfade over two beats. Louder parts make bigger movements, and sharp hits like drums add a small extra curl. All motion is smoothed and capped at 400°/s, and it aims 0.1 s early to make up for delay. It fades in over 3 s while the beat locks, stops when the track ends or on Ctrl-C, and eases back open. Heat: it reads servo temperatures every 3 s, makes the moves smaller above 50 °C and stops at 60 °C. Those two limits are numbers I picked; change them if they're wrong for these servos. Tests: on synthetic beats at 95, 128 and 150 BPM it found the tempo within 1% and the beat within 0.04 of a beat. The mic opens and hears sound. I haven't run it on the real hand with a real song, so please try a full song and say if it's off-beat, too busy or too small. --dry-run just listens and prints BPM, energy and the current move without moving the hand. --routine plays the old fixed routine. The terminal needs Microphone access.

It eases open when the song ends and holds back if the servos get warm. Give it a full song and tell me how the groove feels.

summary: The Dance mode in the Helping Hands Mac app plays what looks like the same fixed move list every time, regardless of the song. The choreography should come from the audio (tempo, beat, loudness, sections, onsets) at the 50% speed cap, so two very different songs produce visibly different motion.
